name: Western Sahara
summary_text: Western Sahara: disputed territory under Moroccan administration: Morocco's criminal law applies plus occupation-era securitisation and no civil space — below even Morocco's own baseline. Scored as a dependent jurisdiction: the parent framework governs what a visitor encounters, plus local society and enforcement. Score re-anchored 2026-09-24: Morocco (0.18) plus a local delta of -0.07. This jurisdiction was not covered by the dedicated state/province research passes.

sources.title: Morocco | Cairo 52 Legal Research Institute
sources.claim_summary: Cairo 52 country review of Morocco (applicable to Western Sahara, a disputed territory administered by Morocco): no specific provisions on transition, but trans people face de facto criminalisation under Article 498 (moral charges, gender-expression discrepancies, involuntary outing); no gender-affirming healthcare framework, leading some to self-medicate; a 2021 legal-recognition process exists for intersex people only; the Grand Mufti opposes transition.

sources.title: Morocco | Outright International
sources.claim_summary: Outright International country overview for Morocco (updated March 2026, applicable to Western Sahara): Article 489 criminalises 'indecent acts' between persons of the same sex (6 months to 3 years), with wide police discretion and arbitrary arrests; 170 people charged with same-sex relations in 2018; HRW documented a 2020 campaign of online harassment of presumed gay and bisexual men; no legal gender recognition; public identification as LGBTIQ carries significant risk of violence and harassment.

sources.title: Morocco/Western Sahara: Activists Need Fair Trial | Human Rights Watch
sources.claim_summary: Human Rights Watch (Dec 2005): 'Morocco/Western Sahara: Activists Need Fair Trial' — urges fair trial for eight jailed Western Saharan human-rights defenders whose case resumed in Laayoune; general rights context under the administering power.

sources.title: Where is it illegal to be gay? A look at all the countries where homosexuality is against the law | PinkNews
sources.claim_summary: PinkNews (July 2017): global roundup of countries where homosexuality is illegal - includes Morocco (which administers Western Sahara) with Articles 489/498, fines and up to 3 years' imprisonment; notes vaguely-worded 'morality' laws and unenforced statutes.

CEAR (Spanish Commission for Refugee Aid) report (Oct 2018, in Spanish): 'Situación del colectivo LGTBI en el Sáhara Occidental' - the legal and social status of LGBTI people in Western Sahara, human-rights violations by state and non-state actors, economic/social/cultural rights, and societal attitudes.

sources.title: The history of LGBTQ+ rights in Spain | Europeana
sources.claim_summary: Europeana story (June 2022): the history of LGBTQ+ rights in Spain - decriminalisation in 1932 under the Second Republic, Lorca's killing, Franco-era persecution (internment camps, jailings), and the post-Franco struggle - historical context for Spain's framework, which applies to Western Sahara's former colonial ties.
